outputs.L1: The present invention relates to a watch-type mobile terminal configured to facilitate the convenient searching of payment cards, coupons, membership cards, and the like used when making payments, and to a method for controlling the same. To achieve the foregoing and other objectives, according to one aspect of the present invention, a watch-type mobile terminal is provided, comprising a display unit, a sensing unit, and a control unit. The control unit is configured to: sense a first input signal associated with payment information displayed on the display unit, the first input signal being a touch input for which at least one of an area or a pressure sensed by the display unit exceeds a predetermined value; display, in response to the first input signal, an indicator or a predetermined item included in the payment information; and enlarge and display the predetermined item in response to a second input signal.
outputs.L2: The invention concerns a watch-style mobile device and a corresponding control method that allow users to easily locate payment-related items, including payment cards, coupons, and membership cards, when making a transaction. To accomplish this and other purposes, one embodiment provides a watch-type mobile terminal having a display, a sensing component, and a controller. The controller detects a first input applied to payment information shown on the display. This input is a touch for which the detected contact area, pressure, or both exceed a preset threshold. In response, the controller presents either an indicator or a specified item contained in the payment information. Upon detecting a second input, the controller magnifies and displays that specified item.
outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a watch-type mobile terminal designed to facilitate the convenient searching and selection of payment-related information, including payment cards, coupons, membership cards, and similar items.

The mobile terminal includes a display unit, a sensing unit, and a control unit. The sensing unit detects touch inputs applied to the display unit, while the control unit processes the detected inputs and controls the information presented on the display.

In particular, the control unit detects a first touch input having a contact area or pressure that exceeds a predetermined threshold. In response to this first touch input, the control unit causes the display unit to present an indicator or highlight a selected item within the available payment-related information. When the sensing unit subsequently detects a second input signal, the control unit enlarges the selected item and displays it in an expanded form, thereby allowing the user to view and access the selected payment card, coupon, membership card, or other payment-related information more easily.
outputs.L4:
A watch-type mobile terminal provides an intuitive interface for quickly searching and selecting payment-related information, including credit or debit cards, coupons, gift cards, membership cards, tickets, and similar items stored in the terminal or an associated account. The terminal includes a touchscreen configured to distinguish touch inputs according to the area of contact, the pressure applied, or both. When a first touch input satisfying a predetermined threshold is detected, the terminal displays a visual indicator, a list of available payment items, or a currently selected item. The user may then browse or change the selected item through additional touch or gesture inputs.

When the terminal detects a second touch input satisfying another predetermined area or pressure threshold, it enlarges the selected payment item or relevant payment information. For example, the terminal may display an enlarged barcode, QR code, card image, account identifier, or other authentication information so that it can be easily presented to and recognized by a payment terminal or scanner. The second input may require a larger contact area or greater pressure than the first input, thereby reducing accidental activation and allowing multiple operations to be performed through a compact watch display.

This staged interaction enables users to locate, confirm, and present payment information with fewer steps and without navigating complex menus. By adapting the displayed content in response to different touch characteristics, the watch-type mobile terminal improves visibility, accessibility, and operational convenience, particularly during time-sensitive payment transactions.
outputs.L5:
### The Power of “The”

“The” is one of the smallest and most frequently used words in the English language. It is known as the definite article and is placed before a noun when referring to something specific. For example, “a book” can mean any book, while “the book” points to a particular one.

Although it contains only three letters, “the” plays an important role in communication. It helps readers and listeners understand whether something is already known, unique, or clearly identified. We say “the sun” because there is only one sun in our solar system, and “the teacher” when both speakers know which teacher is being discussed.

The word may appear simple, but it gives language precision and clarity. Without it, many English sentences would sound unnatural or become more difficult to understand.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for a smartwatch that lets users conveniently search and enlarge payment cards, coupons, and membership cards using pressure-sensitive touch inputs.
counterfactuals.output: A wearable electronic device includes a display, a pressure-sensitive touch input, a memory storing digital representations of transaction cards, coupons, and membership cards, and one or more processors. The processors present a collection of stored items on the display and detect touch inputs having respective locations and pressure levels. In response to a first pressure-sensitive input, the device initiates a search operation or filters the collection based on user-entered criteria. In response to a second pressure-sensitive input directed to a displayed item, the device enlarges at least a portion of the item, including a barcode, account identifier, offer information, or other machine-readable or human-readable content. The amount of enlargement, displayed detail, or search function may be selected according to the detected pressure level or duration. The enlarged item may be presented for optical scanning or contactless payment, thereby enabling efficient retrieval and use of digital cards and offers on a compact wearable display.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a formal invention summary describing a watch-type mobile terminal with a display, sensing unit, and controller for managing payment information through first and second input signals.
counterfactuals.output:
### Invention Summary

The present invention relates to a watch-type mobile terminal configured to facilitate the management and use of payment information. The mobile terminal includes a body wearable on a user’s wrist, a display disposed on the body, a sensing unit configured to detect user inputs, and a controller operatively coupled to the display and the sensing unit.

The controller is configured to display payment information on the display in response to a first input signal detected by the sensing unit. The payment information may include one or more payment instruments, account identifiers, transaction details, or graphical objects corresponding thereto. In response to a second input signal detected while the payment information is displayed, the controller performs a payment-related operation associated with the displayed or selected payment information. The payment-related operation may include selecting a payment instrument, changing payment information, authenticating a user, generating payment data, initiating a transaction, or transmitting payment information to an external payment device.

The first and second input signals may correspond to different touch inputs, gestures, movements, biometric inputs, or combinations thereof. By distinguishing between the input signals, the watch-type mobile terminal enables payment information to be accessed and managed through an intuitive interaction while reducing unintended payment operations and improving transaction security.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a patent specification paragraph for a smartwatch payment interface that uses force-touch gestures to browse cards, coupons, and memberships and zoom in on a chosen item.
counterfactuals.output: A wearable electronic device may provide a payment interface on a touch-sensitive display configured to detect both a contact location and an applied contact force. In response to detecting a force-touch gesture, the device may present a browsable collection of payment items, including payment cards, coupons, tickets, loyalty accounts, and membership credentials. Directional movement of the contact, rotational input, or successive force-touch gestures may navigate among the payment items, while a force exceeding a predetermined threshold on a selected item may enlarge or zoom the selected item to display additional information or controls, such as an account identifier, barcode, expiration date, available balance, reward status, or payment authorization control. The device may vary the zoom level as a function of the detected force and may provide visual, audible, or haptic feedback when navigation, selection, or authorization thresholds are crossed. Upon receiving a confirmation input, the device may authenticate the user and transmit payment or credential data through a short-range wireless interface to a point-of-sale or access-control terminal.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in the style of a translated patent abstract, a watch-type mobile terminal and control method for conveniently searching payment-related items using pressure- or area-based touch sensing.
counterfactuals.output: Disclosed are a watch-type mobile terminal and a control method thereof. The watch-type mobile terminal includes a body wearable on a wrist, a touch screen configured to sense a touch input and at least one of a pressure and a contact area of the touch input, and a controller. When a touch having a pressure or contact area satisfying a preset condition is applied, the controller displays a payment-related item corresponding to the touch. When the sensed pressure or contact area is changed, the controller searches among a plurality of payment-related items and changes the displayed item according to the changed pressure or contact area. Accordingly, a user may conveniently search for and select a card, coupon, membership information, payment history, or other payment-related item by adjusting the force or area of a touch without performing repeated screen-switching operations.
